notify: TU1 adds a distinct usage-accounting domain on the common artifact core; it preserves the existing storage/lifecycle contracts and leaves capture, delivery rollups and UI to TU2–TU5.

flavorEvidence.reasoning: Existing code supplies general artifact storage, journaling, identity and lifecycle hashing. The catalog's common artifact epic owns those generic facilities; its uniform-model/history/feedback stories do not define usage observations, corrections, overlap reconciliation, pending usage attachment or token coverage. TU1 needs multiple accounting stories rather than one extra generic-artifact story. The delivery and model-definition epics address projections and model capabilities, not this domain. Reuse their established boundaries without reopening their generic designs.

analyzeBundles.summary: Exact-file profiles confirmed the artifact store and journal files but returned no indexed entities. Direct reads show an existing durable ArtifactStore and file journal; those are substrate candidates, not evidence that usage-specific appends exist.

Analyzer located ArtifactStore, decodeArtifactHead, createRepoLifecycle, prepareArtifactWrite, artifact contentHash and LLMResponse. It found one prepareArtifactWrite caller and explicitly incomplete graph relationships; affected-writer inventory must be verified rather than inferred from that count.

Bounded document lookup found the common artifact epic's model/store and durable-history designs. Its lifecycle/history/feedback substrate is reused; the new request-usage domain has its own schema, observational semantics and pending attachment contract. Catalog comparison distinguishes delivery projection and model capability work from accounting.
